newsitem.title: UK: Dlr/yen recovers ground on Japan damage limitation.
newsitem.headline: Dlr/yen recovers ground on Japan damage limitation.

text.p: The dollar recovered in Europe, after an overnight stumble to near 114 yen, as Japan sought to calm choppy markets in the wake of surprising comments by Prime Minister Ryutaro Hashimoto over its U.S treasury holdings.

Hashimoto, speaking in New York on Monday, said Japan could be tempted to sell its holdings of U.S. Treasury securities and boost its gold reserves, but had not done so. "I hope the U.S. will engage in efforts and in cooperation to maintain exchange stability so we will not succumb to the temptation to sell off Treasury bills and switch our funds to gold," Hashimoto added.
"If there were to be the threat of selling bonds by the BOJ, it would put upward pressure on the yen," said Daiwa's Fisher.

Daiwa Europe has estimated Japan will invest a potential $180 billion into overseas assets, over 60 percent of that into the U.S., over the next two years. Flows from Japan overseas between 1997 and 2005 are estimated at around $1.6 trillion.
So where to invest if the U.S. Treasuries are no longer an option? Analysts say Japanese stocks and the long-end of the JGB market.
"Longer-term, the big unanswered query is the U.S./Japan trade relation," said David Coleman, chief economist at CIBC Wood Gundy.
